      }, {
        "text": ":34** **Zundamon:** Here, we\u0027ll use the exponential function. The exponential function has the"
      }, {
        "text": " property that it keeps its form when differentiated. So, in the product rule, let\u0027s replace v with an exponential"
      }, {
        "text": " function in advance.\n**9:47** **Metan:** Ah, why is the exponent -x instead"
      }, {
        "text": " of x?\n**9:50** **Zundamon:** You\u0027ll see the reason soon. Now"
      }, {
        "text": ", if we let v be e to the minus x, it looks like this. Notice that a minus sign appeared due"
      }, {
        "text": " to differentiation. And then, if we rearrange the equation, we get this.\n**10:05**"
      }, {
        "text": " **Metan:** Ohh, that\u0027s amazing! Here, u and u\u0027 are treated equally... Although an"
      }, {
        "text": " extra term appeared.\n**10:12** **Zundamon:** We can handle that later."
      }, {
        "text": "\n**10:14** **Metan:** Got it!\n**10:15** **Z"
      }, {
        "text": "undamon:** Now, if we replace u with x^n, we get this equation. Alright, now x^"
      }, {
        "text": "n and x^(n-1) are treated equally. Though the formula is getting a bit complicated...\n**1"
      }, {
        "text": "0:28** **Metan:** That\u0027s true. Let\u0027s simplify the equation a little. Do"
      }, {
        "text": " you notice the same form appearing several times?\n**10:34** **Zundamon:** Uh..."
      }, {
        "text": " yeah, I see it!\n**10:36** **Metan:** So, let\u0027s define"
      }, {
        "text": " g_n(x) like this. Then the left-hand side is just g_n(x). On"
      }, {
        "text": " the right-hand side, we see g_(n-1)(x) and... the derivative of g_n"
      }, {
        "text": "(x).\n**10:50** **Zundamon:** It looks much cleaner now!\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "10:53** **Metan:** To summarize our progress so far... if we define a function g_"
      }, {
        "text": "n(x) like this, it satisfies the following equation.\n**11:00** **Metan"
      }, {
        "text": ":** This is now in a form very close to our target condition!\n**11:04** **Z"
      }, {
        "text": "undamon:** We made a lot of progress! Now then... we need to somehow eliminate the variable x. And that"
      }, {
        "text": " extra term also bothers me.\n**11:12** **Metan:** We can probably handle that by"
      }, {
        "text": " using definite integrals.\n**11:16** **Zundamon:** What? Why does integration suddenly appear"
      }, {
        "text": "? I don\u0027t really get it, but I\u0027ll leave it to you!\n**11:2"
      }, {
        "text": "1** **Metan:** Anyway, let\u0027s try integrating both sides. For now, let\u0027s set the"
      }, {
        "text": " integration interval from a to b, and decide the exact values later.\n**11:29** **Z"
      }, {
        "text": "undamon:** I see, so that\u0027s how it works. Since we integrate with respect to x, the result"
      }, {
        "text": " does not depend on x. Well, that\u0027s fine, but I\u0027m still worried about this extra term."
      }, {
        "text": "\n**11:40** **Metan:** We want that part to become 0. But it\u0027"
      }, {
        "text": "s okay, this definite integral is very easy to handle. Here, since we\u0027re integrating after differentiating, we return"
      }, {
        "text": " to the original function... Then we just need to plug in the values at both ends of the interval.\n**1"
      }, {
        "text": "1:56** **Zundamon:** Got it! We want this value to become 0. So if"
      }, {
        "text": " we pick a and b so that both results become zero, that should be fine.\n**12:04"
      }, {
        "text": "** **Metan:** That sounds good! Let\u0027s try plugging in 0. If we substitute x\u003d0"
      }, {
        "text": " into the definition of g_n(x), it looks like this. Since 0 raised to n is 0"
      }, {
        "text": ", this clearly becomes 0.\n**12:19** **Metan:** We found that plugging in"
      }, {
        "text": " 0 makes the result 0, but what other value would make it 0? This might feel a little sneaky"
      }, {
        "text": "... but let\u0027s try plugging in positive infinity.\n**12:30** **Zundamon:**"
      }, {
        "text": " Infinity?! Are we even allowed to do that?\n**12:33** **Metan:** Plugging in"
      }, {
        "text": " infinity is just shorthand. In reality, it means taking the limit as x goes to infinity. Then, if we move"
      }, {
        "text": " the exponential function to the denominator, since it grows faster than the numerator, the limit goes to 0.\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "12:47** **Zundamon:** Huh, so that\u0027s how you think about it. That"
      }, {
        "text": " means the integration interval should be from 0 to infinity!\n**12:55** **Metan:**"
      }, {
        "text": " Yes!\n**12:56** **Metan:** Okay, let\u0027s integrate both sides again,"
      }, {
        "text": " this time from 0 to infinity. Then it becomes like this. The extra term disappears! Strictly speaking, we should"
      }, {
        "text": " check the convergence of the integral, but let\u0027s skip that for now.\n**13:12**"
      }, {
        "text": " **Zundamon:** Yes, let\u0027s skip it!\n**13:13** **Metan"
      }, {
        "text": ":** The only difference between the two integrals is that n becomes n-1. So if we define the left-hand"
      }, {
        "text": " side as G(n), then the right-hand side can be written as n G(n-1)."
      }, {
        "text": "\n**13:26** **Zundamon:** Oh? Wait a second... We\u0027ve achieved the target"
      }, {
        "text": " condition!\n**13:30** **Metan:** At last, we\u0027ve constructed the function G"
      }, {
        "text": ". G(n) is defined by this definite integral. Written out explicitly, it looks like this.\n**1"
      }, {
        "text": "3:40** **Zundamon:** Oh, there\u0027s one more thing to check. Let\u0027s"
      }, {
        "text": " calculate G(0).\n**13:44** **Metan:** Umm... We just need to consider"
      }, {
        "text": " the case when n \u003d 0. Since x^0 \u003d 1, only e^(-x) remains. Integrating"
      }, {
        "text": " this doesn\u0027t change its form. We just need to be careful about the minus sign. First, as x approaches"
      }, {
        "text": " infinity, e^(-x) becomes 0. When x \u003d 0, e^0 \u003d 1, so"
      }, {
        "text": " the final answer is 1.\n**14:11** **Zundamon:** Great, it turned"
      }, {
        "text": " out to be exactly 1.\n**14:14** **Metan:** In short, if we"
      }, {
        "text": " define G(n) like this... G satisfies the target condition. Therefore, G(n) equals n factorial."
      }, {
        "text": "\n**14:22** **Zundamon:** We finally made it!\n**14:2"
      }, {
        "text": "4** **Metan:** Now, let\u0027s finish this off. We now know that factorials can be expressed"
      }, {
        "text": " using G(n). Based on this, can we extend the factorial?\n**14:34** **"
      }, {
        "text": "Zundamon:** Yes!\n**14:35** **Zundamon:** Since changing the integration variable"
      }, {
        "text": " doesn\u0027t change the value of the definite integral, we can replace x with t. And if we replace n with"
      }, {
        "text": " a real number x, we get this formula!\n**14:47** **Zundamon:** This"
      }, {
        "text": " corresponds to the factorial of x! It is known that this integral converges when x is greater than -1.\n**"
      }, {
        "text": "14:54** **Metan:** Wait! You already knew that?\n**14:56"
      }, {
        "text": "** **Zundamon:** Actually, the Gamma function... the well-known extension of the factorial is offset by"
      }, {
        "text": " 1 in its input.\n**15:03** **Metan:** Oh, I see! Since we"
      }, {
        "text": " shifted x by 1, the domain becomes all positive real numbers.\n**15:09** **Z"
      }, {
        "text": "undamon:** And so, we have arrived at the Gamma function... It is known that the Gamma function has this form"
      }, {
        "text": ".\n**15:16** **Zundamon:** I don\u0027t know why, but I feel"
      }, {
        "text": " like I saw this at the beginning. In fact, its domain can be extended further, even into complex numbers, but"
      }, {
        "text": " let\u0027s end our journey here.\n**15:25** **Metan:** Our journey?"
      }, {
        "text": "\n**15:27** **Zundamon:** To put it simply, the Gamma function is a generalization of"
      }, {
        "text": " the factorial. But keep in mind that it is shifted by 1 compared to the actual factorial. The heart of this"
      }, {
        "text": " definition is the power rule. This is very similar to the property of the factorial, but the key difference is that only"
      }, {
        "text": " the left-hand side is differentiated. To fix that mismatch, we used the product rule. And the exponential function,"
      }, {
        "text": " which keeps its form when differentiated, was helpful here. Finally, by integrating from 0 to infinity, we eliminated the"
      }, {
        "text": " variable t as well as the extra term. This strange integral can be interpreted in this way!\n**16:"
      }, {
        "text": "06** **Metan:** Yeah! But keep in mind, this is just one interpretation.\n**16"
      }, {
        "text": ":10** **Zundamon:** In practice, the Gamma function is rarely derived; most of the time,"
      }, {
        "text": " it is simply given as a definition. Thus, the entire journey we took can be explained with just a few lines of"
      }, {
        "text": " integration by parts. The path to derive it from scratch is tough, but going backwards takes only a moment! Even though"
      }, {
        "text": " the calculation works, it\u0027s not immediately clear what\u0027s going on. That might be one reason why the definition"
      }, {
        "text": " of the Gamma function feels mysterious. Just to be clear, it depends on whether you want an interpretation or just want to"
      }, {
        "text": " state the fact simply.\n**16:44** **Metan:** I see - it\u0027s not"
      }, {
        "text": " about which one is better.\n**16:47** **Zundamon:** This time, what we"
      }, {
        "text": " did was kind of a thought experiment: if someone who didn\u0027t know about the Gamma function tried to reach the generalization"
      }, {
        "text": " of the factorial with minimal background knowledge, what kind of path might be taken?\n**17:01**"
      }, {
        "text": " **Metan:** Huh? That\u0027s what this was?!\n**17:03** **Zund"
      }, {
        "text": "amon:** Please note, we were not explaining the actual history of the Gamma function\u0027s discovery. Still, it wouldn"
      }, {
        "text": "\u0027t be surprising if someone had already walked this path before.\n**17:13** **Zund"
      }, {
        "text": "amon:** Thanks for watching!\n**17:15** **Zundamon:** If you\u0027d like"
      }, {
        "text": " to support this channel, consider becoming a member! In this video, we talk about the purpose of our membership - check"
      }, {
        "text": " it out if you\u0027re interested. Well then, take care, everyone! See you later!"
      }, {

        "thoughtSignature": ""
      }],
